evidence.quote: It is not a condition precedent to payment, and Contractor's obligation to pay for Subcontract Work properly performed is not extinguished if Owner fails to pay for reasons not attributable to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 ties payment to 7 days after Owner payment; Section 6.5 expressly states this is timing only and not a condition precedent.

evidence.quote: within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for that Subcontract Work
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 states seven days after Contractor's receipt of Owner payment.

evidence.quote: Contractor and Subcontractor expressly agree in writing to this payment timing
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 states a specific written payment period.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall retain five percent (5%) of the amount approved for each progress payment as Retainage.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.1 sets 5% retention = 500 bps.

release_condition.value: upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner; also delivery of final waivers (Article 8) and closeout submittals (Article 12)

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release the Retainage to Subcontractor upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 states the two release conditions; Section 7.3 adds final waivers and closeout submittals as further conditions, so clauses must be combined.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay the released Retainage to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after both of those conditions have been satisfied.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 states ten days after both conditions are satisfied.

evidence.quote: With each Application for Payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount requested.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.1.

evidence.quote: Within five (5) days after receipt of each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount received.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2.

evidence.quote: corresponding conditional and unconditional waivers and releases from each of its lower-tier subcontractors and material suppliers whose work or materials are included in the payment
evidence.rationale: Section 8.5 requires lower-tier conditional and unconditional waivers.

evidence.quote: Every waiver and release delivered under this Article shall be in the statutory form prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.4 requires California statutory forms; Section 8.5 extends this to lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment otherwise due to Subcontractor an amount reasonably necessary to protect Contractor against the Defective Work that has not been remedied.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.2 permits withholding for unremedied Defective Work after notice and cure period under 9.1.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not make payment for materials or equipment stored on the Project site or off site.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.6 expressly excludes payment for stored materials, on or off site.

anomalies.description: Retention release is conditioned on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Section 6.5's statement that owner payment is not a condition precedent addresses only the Section 6.4 progress-payment timing. It does not expressly cover retention, so if Owner withholds retention, release could be delayed indefinitely.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release the Retainage to Subcontractor upon Final Completion of the Subcontract Work and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Retention release is conditioned on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Section 6.5's statement that owner payment is not a condition precedent addresses only the Section 6.4 progress-payment timing. It does not expressly cover retention, so if Owner withholds retention, release could be delayed indefinitely.

anomalies.description: Final Completion, a retention release condition, requires closeout submittals to be accepted by Contractor. This is a discretionary trigger within Contractor's control.

evidence.quote: all closeout submittals required by Article 12 have been delivered to and accepted by Contractor
evidence.rationale: Final Completion, a retention release condition, requires closeout submittals to be accepted by Contractor. This is a discretionary trigger within Contractor's control.

anomalies.description: Payment timing runs from Owner's payment. Section 6.5 preserves the obligation if Owner fails to pay, but the contract states no outside date for payment when Owner does not pay.

evidence.quote: The provision in Section 6.4 governs the timing of payment to Subcontractor. It is not a condition precedent to payment
evidence.rationale: Payment timing runs from Owner's payment. Section 6.5 preserves the obligation if Owner fails to pay, but the contract states no outside date for payment when Owner does not pay.

anomalies.description: Payment on termination for convenience is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner. This is owner-contingent payment language outside the progress-payment clause.

evidence.quote: to the extent Contractor recovers those amounts from Owner, but shall not be entitled to anticipated profit on unperformed work
evidence.rationale: Payment on termination for convenience is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner. This is owner-contingent payment language outside the progress-payment clause.

anomalies.description: Delay compensation is available only to the extent Contractor recovers it from Owner; the otherwise exclusive remedy is a time extension.

evidence.quote: unless and to the extent Contractor recovers additional compensation from Owner for that delay on Subcontractor's behalf
evidence.rationale: Delay compensation is available only to the extent Contractor recovers it from Owner; the otherwise exclusive remedy is a time extension.

anomalies.description: The withholding amount is limited to a reasonable amount. The 150% cap applies only 'where required by' Civil Code Section 8814, so its applicability is not fixed by the contract.

evidence.quote: where required by California Civil Code Section 8814, shall not exceed one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the estimated value of the remedial work in dispute
evidence.rationale: The withholding amount is limited to a reasonable amount. The 150% cap applies only 'where required by' Civil Code Section 8814, so its applicability is not fixed by the contract.

anomalies.description: The contract contains no general backcharge or setoff right. Section 6.4 deductions are limited to Retainage and Article 9 defective-work withholdings; controllers should not apply other setoffs on the basis of this document.

evidence.quote: less Retainage under Article 7 and any amount withheld under Article 9
evidence.rationale: The contract contains no general backcharge or setoff right. Section 6.4 deductions are limited to Retainage and Article 9 defective-work withholdings; controllers should not apply other setoffs on the basis of this document.

anomalies.description: Stored materials are not payable on or off site. Materials can be billed only after incorporation into the work.

evidence.rationale: Stored materials are not payable on or off site. Materials can be billed only after incorporation into the work.
